ROOT_CAUSE.my_error: the v1.0 package asserted 'git archive emits GIT BLOB bytes (LF), never the Windows working tree (CRLF)'. That is FALSE for unpinned files. I treated git archive as a blob-faithful exporter when it is a checkout-faithful one, and bound an archive hash on that assumption.
ROOT_CAUSE.proof: the in-archive joint_portfolio.py hashes 7e9b55c3...; LF-normalising those same bytes yields 4efd5739..., which IS the Git blob.
ROOT_CAUSE.verified: all 12 spot-checked files, including all 10 that failed, are now blob-identical
ROOT_CAUSE.what: git archive applied CRLF conversion on export to every file WITHOUT an explicit 'eol=lf' gitattribute. The perfect correlation is the tell: the ONLY files that matched are the ones carrying an eol pin — phase3c/** (pinned earlier) and mr002_development_run.py (pinned by me during Amendment C).
ROOT_CAUSE.why_core_eol_lf_alone_did_NOT_fix_it: core.autocrlf=true OVERRIDES core.eol. Setting only core.eol=lf produced a byte-identical archive (same dd35b845 sha) — a silent no-op that would have looked like a fix.

THE_FAILURE.result: 10 of 20 execution-critical files mismatched their registered Git-blob identities
THE_FAILURE.where: candidate verification, BEFORE the atomic rename — exactly where the owner's staged pattern was designed to catch it

added_verification_step: the candidate check must ALSO assert that no execution-critical file contains CRLF, so a byte mismatch cannot be re-diagnosed from hashes alone
authorizes: NOTHING. Deployment of the corrected package requires a fresh go-ahead; the v1.0 authorization named an archive identity now known to be defective.

boundary.host_state: live tree unchanged; failed candidate and defective archive removed

supersedes.why: its bound archive_sha256 dd35b845... is DEFECTIVE — the archive carries CRLF for every file without an explicit eol pin

\u26a0 WIDER_IMPLICATION.meaning: CRLF hashes have been embedded in governance records before. Package v2.2 already records a SourceIdentityCorrection that fixed 16 such defective identities, all Windows working-tree hashes.
\u26a0 WIDER_IMPLICATION.not_fixed_here: outside this deployment's scope; flagged for a separate sweep.
\u26a0 WIDER_IMPLICATION.observation: 7e9b55c3... — the CRLF hash of joint_portfolio.py — is the value recorded in prior program notes as the governing 'module identity' for the joint construction.
\u26a0 WIDER_IMPLICATION.so_what: this defect class is recurrent and may not be fully eradicated. Any binding derived from a Windows checkout, or from git archive without both flags, is suspect until re-derived from Git blobs.
